input.reason: F08 is confirmed. In src/git-auth.ts:8 the host check is `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")`, which is a plain substring test. `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git` contains that substring, so line 9 returns `-c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer ${token}`. In src/worktree.ts:15, cloneRepo passes those args to `git clone repo.remoteUrl` together with SERVICE_TOKEN, which src/config.ts:4 reads from HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN. Git then sends that header to whatever host the URL names. The remoteUrl comes straight from req.body in routes.ts registerRepo (lines 19-22). That handler only checks that id and remoteUrl are present. It does not validate the URL or its host, and nothing else checks who may register.
input.summary: Substring host check sends the service token to lookalike git remote hosts

findings.text: The host check is a substring match, so a remote URL such as `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git` passes and receives the service token in an `Authorization` header. Any user who can register a repository can collect the token.
findings.reason: Claim 1, that the host check is a substring match: src/git-auth.ts:8 is `if (remoteUrl.includes("github.com"))`. Claim 2, that `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git` passes and receives the token in an Authorization header: that URL contains "github.com", so line 9 returns `["-c", `http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer ${token}`]`. src/worktree.ts:15 passes these args to `git clone repo.remoteUrl` with SERVICE_TOKEN, which src/config.ts:4 sets from HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN. Git therefore sends the header to the attacker's host. Claim 3, that any user who can register a repository can collect the token: src/routes.ts registerRepo takes remoteUrl directly from req.body (line 19). Its only check is that id and remoteUrl are present (line 20). It then calls cloneRepo with that URL (line 22), and no host validation happens anywhere along the way.

input.severity_reason: This is a security flaw that is easy to exploit. Any user who can call registerRepo controls remoteUrl. A lookalike host that contains "github.com" makes the server clone from the attacker's server and send it the GitHub service token as a Bearer header.
